articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Test Socket for Millimeter-Wave Steerable Beam Measurement Technology
abstract: In this study, we present a 2×2 broadband dual-polarized antenna array on the 10 (4+2+4) multi-layer organic substrates with size of 13 × 13 × 0.87 mm3 and measured by test socket. The antenna structure is a stacking patch antenna with parasitic elements, the most suitable substrate stack-up is selected for cost-effectiveness and parasitic elements is added for operation bandwidth enhancement. The test socket is consisted of load board and socket to measure the characteristics of the antenna array. By simulation and optimization, test socket can measure performance close to only antenna array. It's very suitable for quick performance check during R&D phase. In the 24.5 to 29.5 GHz range, the realized gain of antenna array in vertical polarization and horizontal polarization is measured from 9.3 to 11.7 dBi. Finally, the 3D beam steering is implemented in four quadrants at 28GHz, and a maximum realized gain of 8.13dBi is achieved in the beam direction of quadrant IV.

articleTitle: FOWLP-Based Flexible Hybrid Electronics II: Heterogeneous Integration Technology of Micro-LEDs on 3D-IC for Smart Skin Display
abstract: This paper describes heterogeneous integration technologies of micro-LEDs on 3D-IC dielets for Smart Skin Display as a healthcare flexible hybrid electronics (FHE) device to be fabricated based on die-first fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP). Die-level Through-Silicon Via (TSV) formation is demonstrated by spray-coating photolithography and seed-layer deposition with a standard magnetron sputtering system. In addition, SAP (Semi-Additive Plating process) bonding is also demonstrated at room temperature to interconnect the Cu-TSV and Au electrodes on 0.1-mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cubed blue micro-LEDs. This process successfully stacks the micro-LEDs onto the 3D-IC dielet, enabling them to be driven through electroplated Cu pillars. The yield of SAP bonding is enhanced up to over 90% by optimizing the processes using room-temperature OER (ozone-ethylene-radical)-CVD SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and excessive electroplated Cu growth control techniques.

articleTitle: Challenges of Semiconductor Microfabrication Technology for 3D Chiplet Integration
abstract: Chiplet integration technology, which has the potential to scalable expand capabilities by integrating many IC chips with different manufacturing processes, structures, and functions while maintaining the data transfer bandwidth between IC chips, is attracting attention as a promising method to solve the problems such as slowdown of Moore's law and the von Neumann bottleneck. Die-to-die bridge structures that connect dies via locally placed bridge chips with high-density interconnects is expected for scalable chiplet integration. In this paper, we propose plasma etching technologies to realize novel die-to-die bridge architecture called “Pillar-Suspended Bridge (PSB)”, and new through-silicon via etching technologies for 3D-IC integration, as well.

articleTitle: Template Stripping of Au from Polyimide Film for Smoothing of Bonding Surface
abstract: Surface roughness is dominant in the low temperature bonding. Here, we present the template stripping (TS) technique using polyimide film for smoothing the A<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u$</tex> surface. By repeating the TS process, the rough surface became smooth.

articleTitle: Suppression of Surface Roughening of Ag Films by Capping Layer for Ag/Ag Surface Activated Bonding
abstract: A titanium layer (thickness: 2 nm) has been used as a capping layer to suppress the surface roughening of silver (Ag) thin films (thickness: 30 nm) for Ag-Ag surface activated bonding at room temperature.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Expansion of a Testing Station Using a 0.3-mm-Pitch LGA Interface for a $25\text{-Gbaud} \times 16- \text{Channel}$ CPO Transceiver
abstract: This paper describes the design and transmission characteristics of a bandwidth-expanded testing station using a 0.3-mm-pitch LGA-based electrical pluggable interface for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{25}- \mathbf{Gbaud} \times \mathbf{16}-\mathbf{channel}$</tex> optical transceiver. This testing station employs a core-less building-up multi-layer organic substrate to avoid impedance mismatch at the vias in a core layer. Densely placed electrical connectors are used to shorten the length of electrical transmission lines. This testing station has a 3-dB bandwidth of 17.3 GHz, which is sufficient for 25-Gbaud signal transmission. We also build an optical link by attaching a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{28}- \mathbf{Gbaud} \times \mathbf{8}-\mathbf{channel}$</tex> optical transceiver on the testing station to evaluate signal transmission characteristics. When operating the optical link by 28-Gbaud NRZ signals, a measured jitter margin at BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup> is as wide as 0.49 UI. which is 0.12 UI. larger than that of using our previously fabricated testing station.

articleTitle: Packaging of SiC Power Module with a Low-Permittivity Material to Reduce Capacitive Coupling
abstract: This study proposes a new power module configuration to reduce CM noise. The proposed module utilized a low permittivity material which replaces a part of bottom Cu layer. The design scheme does not sacrifice thermal performance and the size of power module remains the same. The power module does not experience a reduction in break-down voltage by the proposed design. The parasitic CM capacitance is reduced by 42% compared to that of the conventional module. Detailed explanations about packaging method for the proposed power module are also presented.

articleTitle: Schottky Barrier Diode Based on Ge-Doped $\alpha-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ Films Grown by Mist-CVD Method
abstract: We fabricated Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) based on Ge-doped <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\alpha}-\mathbf{Ga}_{\mathbf{2}}\mathbf{O}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> films grown by mist-CVD method. The transfer length methods (TLM) were performed for Ti/Au and Ti/Al/Ti/Au electrodes before and after rapid thermal annealing (RTA) to confirm ohmic contact and to estimate the sheet and contact resistance. For both electrodes, the RTA was found to be effective to improve the ohmic characteristics. For SBD with Ti/Al/Ti/Au ohmic electrode for which RTA was carried out at 450 °C, the ideality factor, the barrier high and the on-resistance were estimated to be 1.10, 1.01 eV and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}.\mathbf{9}\ \mathbf{m}\mathbf{\Omega}\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>, respectively. The analysis on resistance of n-drift layer as well as sheet and contact resistance of n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> layer clarifies that the on<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> resistance is mainly governed by the sheet and contact resistance for the present SBD.

articleTitle: A Record High Optical Output Power Pigtailed-OSFP External Laser Source for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: This paper describes a design and characteristics of a record high optical output power pigtailed-OSFP ELS employing an uncooled 8-channel CWDM TOSA for Co-Packaged Optics. An OSFP housing has a bigger mechanical size compared with a QSFP housing and thus an OSFP housing accept increasing power consumption to obtain higher optical output power. Based on thermal simulations, characteristics of LD temperature and case temperature of the TOSA are anticipated with an ambient temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40{}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex> and an air flow rate of 3.75 CFM. The maximum LD temperature is as high as 620 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mA}$</tex> to keep an LD temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 65\ {}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>. To output record fiber-coupled optical power of 22 dBm per channel, a required LD bias current is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 550$</tex> mA, whereby power consumption and a PCE are 10.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}$</tex> and 12.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: Development of High Heat-Resistant Multilayer Barrier Electrodes Suitable for Multiple Reflow Processes
abstract: Various barrier layers were introduced to suppress electrode dissolution; among them, the molybdenum (Mo) barrier electrode maintained high shear strength after multiple reflow cycles because of the formation of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\beta}-\mathbf{Sn}$</tex> layer at the solder interface.

articleTitle: Simulation Method of 32Gbps Signal Transmission Considering Xtalk Impact Using Probability Density Function
abstract: PCIe® Gen5 transmission is verified through eye analysis using the S-parameters of the channel. However, since the physical properties of connectors used in actual devices are unknown, modeling them with a 3D electromagnetic field tool and creating S-parameters becomes challenging. For this reason, it is necessary to obtain the S-parameter through actual measurements, including the substrate used in the channel. However, network analyzers capable of measuring multi-ports, including crosstalk ports, are expensive, so S-parameters including the crosstalk characteristics of the connector cannot be easily acquired. In this study, we propose a simple method to evaluate the effect of crosstalk using the standard deviation values distributed in the voltage probability density function of a signal waveform and crosstalk waveforms. The distinctive feature of this method is that it relies on only 4-port S-parameters, which can be easily measured. We compared the eye aperture using the proposed method with the 24-port S-parameters and confirmed that crosstalk can be evaluated with a difference of 0.4 mV and 0.7 ps.

articleTitle: Inductive Sintering Module for Improved Multi-Die Attach in the Field of Power Packaging
abstract: This work presents a heating technology for multi-die attach based on inductive silver sintering. Thus, the heat for the sintering reaction is confined locally to the bond region, avoiding heating of the entire power module.

articleTitle: Polymer Optical Waveguide Coupler with Vertically Bent Cores
abstract: In this paper, polymer optical waveguides with 90-degree bent GI cores are fabricated using the Mosquito method. Material combinations that allow the formation of GI cores even with a diameter as large as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{70}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \boldsymbol{m}$</tex> are screened. By further adjusting the interim time, the desired parabolic GI core can be fabricated to realize a low-loss coupling device.

articleTitle: A 3.6-4.5 GHz Doherty RF Power Amplifier Using $0.25-\mu \mathrm{m}$ GaN/SiC HEMT and GaAs IPD Technology
abstract: This paper introduces a Quasi-MMIC Doherty power amplifier operating in the 3.6-4.5 GHz frequency range. The power amplifier was manufactured using WIN™ Semiconductors' <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.25}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> Gallium Nitride/Silicon Carbide (GaN/SiC) technology and GaAs IPD technology. The GaN and GaAs IPD chips for the proposed power amplifier were assembled using Chip-on-Board wire-bond assembly technology. The power amplifier exhibited a gain of 18.5 dB, a 3-dB bandwidth from 3.6 GHz to 4.5 GHz, a saturation power of 38.4 dBm, and a peak power-added efficiency of 32.8%. In the context of a 5G NR FR1 256-QAM modulated signal with a 100-MHz bandwidth, the power amplifier demonstrated an average output power of 29.9 dBm under an error vector magnitude 3.5% limitation.

articleTitle: Influence of EMC Tg on Leakage Current in HTRB Test and Delamination in MSL Test for Power Package
abstract: High Tg EMC is more robust in HTRB Test for power package but exhibits high delamination in MSL Test. Polyimide (PI) coating shows significant improvement on high Tg EMC delamination in MSL.

articleTitle: Metal-Polymer Direct Joining Using Small Textures on Metal Surface
abstract: The direct metal-polymer joining method using small textures on metal surface and injection molding is described. As a metal surface treatment, we here introduce hot water treatment, a simple, inexpensive, and chemical-free method. Strong joints with tensile shear strength of more than 20 MPa were obtained between aluminum and galvanized steel, and PBT when the hot water treatment and injection molding conditions are appropriately set. XPS analysis on the treated metal surface and cross-sectional analysis via TEM supported that the joining is derived from mechanical interlocking with these materials. We would like to promote the implementation of this technology in various industries, such as automotive, medical, and semiconductor packaging.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Mitigation for High Speed SerDes Applications on FCBGA Package
abstract: Flip-chip ball grid array (FCBGA) is a good and popular package solution for high speed serializer/ deserializer (SerDes) applications. However, the crosstalk performance gets worse at higher frequency, especially a 64 GHz peak is usually observed. Many substrate design components will affect electrical performance, such as package thickness, material, ball size, void size, and routing topology. This paper investigates several design schemes to mitigate the peak of crosstalk issue. The simulation results show that both far-end crosstalk (FEXT) and near-end crosstalk (NEXT) can be significantly improved by 10.9 dB and 4.0 dB, respectively. Signal integrity of high data rate signals can be optimized consequently by applying those design factors.

articleTitle: Packaging of a 25-Tiles Device on Large Dimension AlN Ceramic Substrate Keeping Low Dead Areas and Tight Planarity
abstract: Chiplet architecture technologies, in addition to expanding computing resources, is also applicable to high-resolution optical sensors development, meeting low dead areas and good planarity on the whole focal plane. While choosing a monolithic solution soon leads to yield issues, we explored a packaging solution with 25 chips butted in an array on a ceramic substrate. Many challenges were addressed: first, minimizing the distance between chips, in order to keep a constant pitch on a chip and in between chips; second, controlling the bonding position of each chip to ensure a good planarity on the whole focal plane. In addition, a specific design work was provided to ensure a good signal integrity on the ceramic package. Finally, temperature modelisations were made to optimize the design of the ceramic package and extract correctly the heat on the backface.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Integrated Photonics for Future Optical Interconnects and Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to introduce some of the technological breakthroughs in heterogeneous III-V/Si phase tuners which can be used for both ultra-energy efficient data transmission and photonic neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Coupling Loss from SMF to Polymer Optical Waveguides with Various Refractive Index Profiles
abstract: In this paper, we theoretically estimate the temperature dependence of coupling loss between single-mode (SM) polymer optical waveguides and general-purpose SM fiber (SMF), and discuss about the applicability of polymer optical waveguides to co-packaged optics (CPO). Although SM polymer optical waveguides are expected to be applied as an element of CPO, their small cores require precise mode-field adjustment with precise alignment of the cores. The mode-field and alignment positions of polymer waveguides are conce1ed to be affected by their operation temperature, particularly when integrated with Si photonics chips that could be a heat source. Simulation results show that the properties are maintained even under high-temperature operation.

articleTitle: A Study on the Inductance and Thermal Regression and Optimization for Automatic Layout Design of Power Modules
abstract: Power modules with excellent inductance and temperature metrics are significant to meet the rising sophistication of energy demand in new technologies. In this paper, we use a surrogate-based approach to render optimal layouts of power modules with feasible and attractive inductance-temperature ratios at low computational budget. In particular, we use the class of feedforward networks to estimate the surrogate relationships between power module layout-design variables and inductance-temperature factors rendered from simulations; and Differential Evolution algorithms to optimize and locate feasible layout configurations of power module substrates minimizing inductance and temperature ratios. Our findings suggest the desirable classes of feedforward networks and gradient-free optimization algorithms being able to estimate and optimize power module layouts efficiently and effectively.

articleTitle: Polymer Spot Size Expander on Laser Diode Chip for Fiber Coupling
abstract: A miniaturized polymer spot size expander was successfully applied using UV-curable resin on the end face of a DFB laser diode chip emitting at 1.31 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> wavelength for the first time. The spot size could be expanded from the original 3.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> to 5.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The coupling efficiency with a single mode fiber was improved to be −1.2 dB from −3.3 dB, and 3-dB down positional tolerance along the optical axis was improved to be bigger than 60 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> from 20 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> without SSE.

articleTitle: Polishing of CVD Diamond for Direct Bonding Using Ar and SF6-Gas Cluster Ion Beams
abstract: CVD diamond for direct bonding were polished using Ar and SF6-gas cluster ion beam (GCIB). The effects of gas variety on the removed thickness, surface roughness and the crystallinity of diamond surface were discussed. Results show that diamond was etched faster by SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-GCIB than by Ar-GCIB with the same ion dose and acceleration voltage. For a smooth diamond surface, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-GCIB irradiation could decrease the surface roughness and smooth the surface further by increasing the ion dose. Most importantly, additional damages were not induced during this process. But it could not change the morphology of the diamond surface. While after Ar-GCIB irradiation, wave patterns on diamond surface disappeared with the sacrifice of a smooth surface, and the crystallinity of the diamond became poor.

articleTitle: Polymer Optical Waveguide Type 3-D MUX Device for Mode Division Multiplexing Links
abstract: Using the Mosquito method, we fabricate waveguides with 3-dimensionally arranged cores to be applied to a MUX device for mode-division multiplexing technology. Applying the developed MUX, the different higher-order modes, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11a</inf> and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11b</inf> in one few-mode fiber core can be individually excited.

articleTitle: Structural Investigation of Rare-Earth Metal Polymer Composite Doped Optical Amplifiers for Higher Gain
abstract: Embedded optical waveguides with a circular core doped with europium (Eu)-aluminum (Al) polymer composite are fabricated using the Mosquito method, and the relationship between the core diameter and amplification gain is investigated. Further increase in gain is expected by setting up the amplification measurement system appropriately for waveguides with large core diameters.

articleTitle: Photonic System-in-Package (pSiP) by Applying Thin Glass
abstract: Advanced photonic System-in-Package (pSiP) technologies are proposed to enhance functionality of photonic packages featuring electrical, thermal and optical components including laser diodes, modulators, isolators, PIC, beam-splitters and micro lenses. We discuss thin glass as a suitable base material for packages made on panel level, precise glass structuring, optical waveguide integration, electrical wiring and the related high precision assembly techniques.

articleTitle: 350°C Operation of SiC Complementary JFET Logic Gates
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) complementary junction field-effect transistor (CJFET) assembled with p-and n-channel JFETs were fabricated by ion implantation. The SiC CJFET inverter operates from 300 to 623 K with a 1.4 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: High Density Automotive Module with Fan-Out Package
abstract: In accordance with widespread of connected cars and autonomous driving, automotive SoCs (System-on-Chips) are required to have high-performance computing and high-speed transmission. As a result, requirements for package level heterogeneous integration have been increasing. However, 2.5D packaging structure is complicated and challenging to control manufacturability. This paper demonstrates a redistribution layer design, module substrate design, low power double data rate 4 (LPDDR4) electrical verification and reliability testing of a high-density multi-chip module with fan-out package.

articleTitle: High Density Optical Transceiver Packaging Using Glass Substrates and Through Glass Vias
abstract: Through glass vias (TGV) are an emerging technology that enables electrical interposers with advantages over organic substrates. These advantages include excellent dimensional stability, a coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) more closely matched with silicon dies, high thermal stability and high electrical isolation. These are all beneficial to the increased data rates that are required in modern systems. In addition, TGV can be beneficial for optical transceiver packaging design that supports higher data rates as well as higher densities. We describe the benefits of TGV technology in the design of an optical engine capable of supporting 112 Gbps channels with industry-leading density.

articleTitle: Development of Adapter-Less Compact Multifiber Optical Connector
abstract: The newly developed adapter-less compact multifiber optical connector (MTCT® connector) can provide two times higher density than the MPO connector. The performance of this connector is comparable with the standard MPO connector.

articleTitle: Nb-Nb Direct Bonding Pads for Superconducting Devices and Their Failure Mode
abstract: Direct bonding of Nb was performed for 3D integration of superconducting devices. Electrical properties and superconducting transition temperatures were measured to investigate the effect of fast atomic beam on the bonding interface.

articleTitle: Development of a Highly Porous Polycaprolactone (PCL) Microneedles Array Patch to Improve the Absorption of Interstitial Fluid (ISF)
abstract: In recent years, microneedle (MN) technology has attracted attention as a sensing tool for the extraction of interstitial fluid (ISF) that has various biomarkers related to our health, and analysis of such biomarkers. In our previous study, we developed a porous microneedles array patch (MAP) made of low-melting point polycaprolactone (PCL), cellulose fibers, and polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a porogen. However, there were some issues such as less porous structure on the surface of MN and defects including cracks in MN. As a result, there were several concerns that the sensing accuracy would decrease, and that the tip of the MN might remain in the skin causing inflammation during skin puncture. To solve these issues, in this study, we develop new porous MNs uisng high molecular weight of PCL with NaCl as a porogen with controlling particle sizes. By selecting a particle size of 5 μm with a NaCl content of 70%, our new MAP achieved more pores on the surface of MN and the higher mechanical strength of MN. Furthermore, we conducted animal experiments using the new porous PCL-MAP and achieved better ISF absorption performance as well as glucose sensing ability after skin puncture. From the results, it is expected that our new porous PCL-MAP can be a practical glucose sensing tool, for example, for prediabetic patients.

articleTitle: Demonstration of High-Power Stability of Polymer Optical Waveguides Using External Laser Source (ELS) for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: We demonstrate high-power stability of polymer optical waveguide using external laser source. No noticeable loss for short-term continuous input of total optical power of +24.6 dBm with 4-wavelength WDM to the polymer waveguide.

articleTitle: Sampling of Biological Interstitial Fluid by Porous Microneedle Array Patches
abstract: Interstitial fluid (ISF) that can be extracted from the skin contains various biomarkers related to health care as well as early diagnosis. Recently, porous Microneedle Array Patch (MAP) has been developed as a tool to analyze glucose concentration by extracting ISF from the body instead of traditional blood sampling [1]. In this study, we developed porous MAP to extract ISF for the analysis of various biomarkers included in ISF. In detail, the configuration of the porous MAP was revised in order to quickly separate the absorbing parts from the tape after ISF absorption. In our previously developed MAP configuration, the high adhesion between the surgical tape and the sensor sheet or microneedle made it impossible to separate them, including the ISF [2]. Thus, we developed a new configuration in which a removable tape and PET film are inserted between the surgical tape and the microneedles so that the sensing part including ISF can be separated as soon as the absorption of the ISF is completed. In addition, we changed the material of sensing part that mainly absorbs ISF, from the previous paper sheet to a non-woven fabric to improve the absorbency. With the new configuration, we performed puncture tests on agarose gels as well as even rats' skin, and confirmed the amount of ISF absorbed and the improved disassembly capability of the porous MAP. The puncture test on rats also confirmed that there was no damage to the skin. Finally, the stable sampling of the ISF amount for analysis is still a further issue, and we will make further improvements by introducing, for instance, an applicator to reduce the pressure difference when being applied to the skin during ISF absorption.

articleTitle: Tactile Pressure Sensor Based on Flexible Polymer Optical Waveguides Fabricated by the Mosquito Method
abstract: In this paper, a polymer-based optical waveguide sensor is created to address several issues in optical fiber-based sensors. The unique feature of our optical waveguide is its 3-D core arranged design fabricated using the Mosquito method to which poly dimethyl siloxane (PDMS) is applied as the cladding for a flexible tactile sensor. The core monomer is dispensed into the PDMS monomer to have a 3D lattice structure. We demonstrate that the fabricated waveguide sensors exhibit a high repeatability of the pressure sensing. We find that the measurement range is from 0 MPa to 0.164 MPa when an organic inorganic hybrid resin, NP-C01-KO is used as the main core material. By examining the effect of the numerical aperture and the core size on the sensitivity, we confirm that bending loss could cause the output power variation when a load is applied to the sensor.

articleTitle: Unique Optical Connect Structure with Polymer Waveguide Fabricated by the Mosquito Method
abstract: We develop a unique optical connect structure with polymer waveguide fabricated by the Mosquito method for Co-Packaged Optics. We present the details of this optical connect structure and evaluation results of prototype waveguide.

articleTitle: Prototyping and Evaluation of SiC Half Bridge Circuit Using Power Device Embedded Module Process Towards Future Three Dimensional Packaging
abstract: Recently WBG (Wide Band Gap) power semiconductors such as SiC and GaN, which have been attracting attention, are being applied in power electronics field because of their high switching speed and low losses compared to existing Si power devices. SiC is spreading from industrial applications to main traction systems of N700S SHINKANSEN bullet trains, and GaN is spreading to low-voltage applications such as AC adapters, DC/DC converters and LED drivers etc. . On the other hand, there are problems such as surge noise due to current path stray inductance Ls by high current reduction rate, di/dt, at turn-off. To reduce the turn-off voltage surge, it is necessary to optimize structure of main current path to minimize Ls. In optimizing the structure, loop inductance can be reduced by forming a return path in which current distribution could cancels leakage magnetic flux. However, depending on the switching mode of the power converter topology, such as a three phase inverter, the main current may not always be a return path that cancels the leakage magnetic flux. This time, in order to confirm the usefulness of Power Device Embedded Module (POWER DEM) packaging process, a prototype of SiC bare die embedded half-bridge circuit has been prototyped. Inductance analyzed results of circuit structure using ANSYS Q3D Extractor® before prototyping, have been comparatively evaluated. As a result, loop inductance was 5.5 nH in Q3D analysis, 3.6 nH in impedance analyzer, and calculated inductance from actual surge voltage was 10.03 nH. Finally, turn-off voltage surge, turn-on loss, turn-off loss, turn-on time and turn-off time have been reduced approximately 40 % to 80 % compared to similar half bridge circuit using conventional TO-247 packages. Further works are to optimize current path constructions for actual cases of circuit topologies i.e. three phase inverter etc., modeling of three dimensional structure including dielectric insulating material and analyze methods.

articleTitle: Multi Die Stacked Structure Fabricated by WoW Bonding
abstract: To achieve 2-die stacking process, fusion bonding technology was applied for Wafer on Wafer (WoW) by each oxide film, and Through Silicon Via (TSV) was used to connect metal layer in each wafer. Electrical characteristics was evaluated to confirm the connection. We also introduced the case study of 4-die stacking using the 2-die stacking technology.

articleTitle: A DfT Technique for Electrical Interconnect Testing of Circuit Boards with 3D Stacked SRAM ICs
abstract: A Design-for-test (DfT) technique is proposed in this paper for a test method, by which detecting open defects occurring interconnects between 3D stacked SRAM IC and a printed circuit board and among dies inside them. The test method is based on the supply current that is made flow through an interconnect to be tested. The DfT technique utilizes a built-in current sensor circuit to detect the open defects. It is shown that open defects occurring at interconnects among dies designed by the DfT method in a 3D stacked SRAM IC, and between the IC and a circuit board can be detected by the supply current test method.

articleTitle: FOWLP-based Flexible Hybrid Electronics I: Photobiomodulation Device Fabrication on Hydrogel Substrate Using RDL-first Approach
abstract: This paper focuses on the fabrication of a PhotoBioModulation (PBM) device as a kind of flexible hybrid electronics (FHE) with a hydrogel substrate. PBM is a type of phototherapy using visible or near-infrared (NIR) light from LEDs or lasers. We propose an integrated PBM patch using RDL (redistribution layer)-first fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP) with an array of embedded NIR mini-LEDs in the hydrogel as a substrate for chronic wound or bedsore healing. This paper characterizes the fan-out wirings formed on the hydrogel and describes multichip-to-wafer bonding with the mini-LEDs.

articleTitle: Understanding Design Rules of Fan-in WLCSP Concerning Thermo-Mechanical Challenges
abstract: Wafer Level Chip Scale Packaging (WLCSP) is a type of chip packaging technology that allows for the integration of multiple semiconductor devices on a single wafer. This is achieved by using a wafer-level process to package the chips directly onto the wafer surface, eliminating the need for a separate package. It offers several advantages over traditional packaging methods, such as smaller size; improved thermal performance; lower cost and higher density. As a result, it is becoming increasingly popular in the semiconductor industry. While WLCSP solution offers numerous benefits, it also presents some challenges in terms of mechanical reliability. The absence of a separate package in WLCSP makes the chips more vulnerable to physical damage, such as cracking or chipping, during handling or assembly. The solder joints used to connect the chip to the external components can create stress concentration points on the chip, which can lead to die cracking or other types of damage. Package level qualification tests for the assessment of component reliability may cause delamination and cracking of the die active layer as well as re-passivation, which is essential of the WLCSP process for re-routing. These cracks could expose the die to the environment, which can lead to corrosion and other long term reliability issues in its field service. This paper addresses such problems as re-passivation and die active layer cracking in a systematical way and comes up with a general guideline of design rules aiming at enhancing its integrity during the package level qualification. The impact of geometry and process related variables is evaluated using the general-purpose finite element code ANSYSY Mechanical in terms of relevant stress components. It is found that simulation results are in good agreement with failure analysis observations regarding the cracking initiation and propagation. Detailed numerical studies and discussions are presented about the re-passivation termination structures, die corner configurations, space between the openings of the first and second re-passivation layer as well as re-passivation thickness and its curing process.

articleTitle: Development of Anti-ESD Backgrinding Tape
abstract: We developed an Anti-ESD backgrinding(BG) tape to introduce an Anti-Statics (AS) layer between the substrate and adhesive layer. With the BG tape, peeling charge was reduced by 98% without an ionizer compared to the conventional tape.

articleTitle: Printable Sheet Sensor System with Organic Circuit for Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: Sensor systems with independent power supplies are increasingly in demand for monitoring the health of aging infrastructure. We developed a self-powered sheet-type sensor system using scalable and printable strain sensors and organic circuits.

articleTitle: Ceramic-Packaged Multichip Front-End Module for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: A low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC)-packaged multichip front-end module is proposed for the applications of the fifth generation (5G) millimeter wave mobile communications. The front-end is comprised of 4 channels and each channel integrates one antenna, one coupler, one image rejection mixer (IRM), two bandpass filters (BPFs) and two amplifiers. The module down-converts 28 GHz signal to 0.5 GHz, and the measured gain, noise figure (NF) and image rejection are better than 35 dB, 3.3 dB and 20 dB, respectively. The module also presents large scale integration and possesses a small size of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{40}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{30}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{1}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Warpage Observation of Liquid Compression Mold Underfill on Strip Substrate
abstract: Liquid Compression Mold Underfill (LCMUF) is a liquid encapsulation material that was developed to encapsulate wafer-level packages of 12-inch silicon wafers using a compression molding machine. In this report, we applied it to a package of FR-4 strip substrate using a compression molding machine for wider application of LCMUF. To encapsulate the strip substrate, the process used Mold Underfill (MUF) with a transfer molding machine is commonly applied. In comparison, the compression molding process with LCMUF has the advantages of waste reduction of encapsulation material, low risk of chip misalignment, low heat damage to mounted components, and good flowability to chip gaps. On the other hand, since the warpage of the strip substrate after molding may cause problems during subsequent processes, such as grinding and dicing, it is essential to reduce the warpage of the strip substrate. Therefore, we optimized the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) property of LCMUF and succeeded in reducing the warpage of the strip substrate after compression molding. Moreover, this LCMUF also shows good flowability to chip gap between mounted chip and strip substrate uniformly without voids.

articleTitle: Jitter Margin Analysis of 56-Gb/s $\text{PAM}4\times 8-\text{Channel}$ VCSEL-Based Optical Transceiver for Co-Packaged Optics
abstract: We evaluate an optical link employing an ultra-compact 850-nm MM VCSEL-based 56-Gb/s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{PAM}\mathbf{4} \times \mathbf{8}-\mathbf{channel}$</tex> optical transceiver and three different kinds of MMFs (i.e., OM3, OM4, and OM5 fibers). We particularly analyze jitter margin characteristics for serial and 8-channel parallel signal transmissions. TDECQ values are also measured for optical eye diagrams transmitted through MMFs of several different conditions. The measured TDECQ values are as small as <1.9 dB within the specified distances of MMFs based on IEEE802.3cm. Jitter margin characteristics at the KP4-FEC threshold (i.e., BER of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}.\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{4}})$</tex> are narrower as increasing the distance of OM4, but a jitter margin of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{35}$</tex> U.I. can be kept within 110 m. We also measure no jitter margin degradation between serial and 8-channel parallel signal transmissions.

articleTitle: Low Loss Design and Fabrication for Tapered Waveguide Based Spot Size Converter
abstract: In this paper, propagating mode analysis is performed to optimize the core cross-sectional shape of polymer optical waveguide to be applied to a low loss adiabatic coupler to Si photonics chips when it is fabricated using the Mosquito method.

articleTitle: Retroreflection Using Bloch Surface Wave Resonance for External Laser Mirror
abstract: A narrowband retroreflector consisting of a dielectric multilayer is designed for both retroreflecting a diverging incident wave from a semiconductor optical amplifier and supporting a Bloch surface wave. The retroreflectance is predicted to be 56%.

articleTitle: Pillar-Cavity Copper-Copper Bonding for Face-to-Face Carbon Nanotube Synthesis
abstract: The bonding process is a critical step in the synthesis of face-to-face interlaced carbon nanotubes. Copper-copper bonding has emerged as a promising alternative to traditional silicon dioxide to silicon dioxide bonding due to its advantages, including a reduced bonding area requirement and greater flexibility in chip-to-chip bonding. However, the use of formic acid in copper-copper bonding can adversely affect the catalyst employed in carbon nanotube synthesis. This paper presents a modified technique for achieving high-quality Cu-Cu bonding without the need for formic acid. We introduce the innovative use of pillar-cavity pairs, designed to increase contact pressure at the Cu-Cu interface during the bonding process. Additionally, a copper base is employed to enhance the adhesion strength between the electroplated copper pillars and the substrate. Our experimental results demonstrate that the bonded chips can withstand subsequent processes, including double-side-dicing and high-temperature treatments, highlighting the robustness of this bonding approach. The bonding strength is quantitatively evaluated through shear tests, confirming the reliability and stability of the Cu-Cu bonds formed using this technique. This technology exhibits promising potential for use in the future synthesis of face-to-face interlaced carbon nanotubes.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Reduction in Ultra-High-Density High-Speed Optical Receiver
abstract: We developed an ultra-compact CPO transceiver module in the size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.8\times 16\times 8.0$</tex> for 400 Gb/s, 25 Gbps NRZ × 16-channel. To minimize the CPO transceiver, we adopted a MCF with a hexagonal close-packed core at a pitch of 40 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> and an optical device array with the same arrangement. The optical transceiver module consists of a bottom-emitting 16-channel TCC-VCSEL array, a back-illuminated 16-channel PD array, a driver array, and a TIA array. A 16-channel MCF is used for each optical interface of transmitter and receiver, and a high-density LGA of 0.3 mm pitch is used for the electrical interface. We applied quasi differential wiring between PD array and TIA array to suppress the crosstalk in ultra-high-density and high-speed CPO optical receiver. By adopting the quasi-differential wiring, the receiver sensitivity at a BER <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=10^{-12}$</tex> were −9.0 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dBm}$</tex> without crosstalk, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-8.7\ \text{dBm}$</tex> with crosstalk from three adjacent channels. It was confirmed that crosstalk could be suppressed to 0.3 dB even in the 40 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> pitch ultra-high-density optical receiver.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Multimode Polymer Optical Waveguide Based Splitter by the Mosquito Method and Investigation of Its Signal Splitting Ratio
abstract: In this paper, multimode Y-branched waveguides with low insertion losses are designed and fabricated applying our original fabrication method of polymer optical waveguides named the Mosquito Method, and then, light splitting ratios of the fabricated Y-branched waveguides are investigated for application to DEMUX devices.

articleTitle: Abnormal Position Identification Technique for Communication Channels Using Adaptive DFE
abstract: In today's advancing era of autonomous driving, invehicle systems have to perform self-diagnosis and maintenance to operate vehicles for longer periods. Since In-vehicle communication channels are longer than ten meters, the problem of the maintenance is that the replacement of components takes time and costly. Diagnosing abnormal locations in communication channels is required to operate maintenances efficiently. In this paper, we demonstrated that abnormal locations of communication channels can be identified by using tap coefficients of an adaptive decision feedback equalizer (DFE). Considering DFE with over 100 taps is unrealistic, we convolute the data on DFE tap coefficients obtained at various transmission start times, which results in pulse response with a peak at the abnormal location. In this approach, we achieved abnormal location diagnosis with a resolution of 0.2 m by using five taps of DFE in bidirectional communication at 1 Gbps. This enables the replacement of only the faulty components at the maintenance of communication channels.

articleTitle: Study of Nitride Crack Reduction For Electronic Power Devices
abstract: This research uses Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to study the impact of different factors on SiN passivation stress in power MOSFETs during Temperature Cycling (TC) lifetest, including power metal thickness, different clip designs, and EMC selection. The FEA results are also compared with TC results obtained from experiments.

articleTitle: Board-Level Drop Reliability Analysis for Fine-Pitch BGA Packages in Automotive Applications
abstract: As the demand of automotive application grown-up rapidly, electronic packages are required zero defect after manufacturing and ultra-high performance from package level to board-level reliability tests. Since automotive packages operate in dramatic temperature ranges, solder joint combination is recommended chosen high Ag lead-free solder alloy to greatly enhance the fatigue life of the board-level temperature cyclic test (TCT) performance. However, high Ag lead-free solder alloy will lower reliability of drop performance. Solder alloy selection is a key issue and trade-off for automotive application. The board-level drop reliability performance is now facing the big challenge. In this work, we would like to focus on board-level drop performance enhancement. The common package type, fine-pitch ball grid array (BGA) is widely used as automotive component. The body size of test vehicle is selected in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20} \times \mathbf{20}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>. Both experiment and numerical model were investigated to analyze board-level drop reliability of the package. The board-level drop experiment was followed JEDEC JESD22-B111A with impact profile 1500 G & 0.5 ms. A three-dimension finite element method (FEM) was used to evaluate the stress level comparison and comes out design guideline under drop test. The real-time strain response on test board between experiment and modeling are well-correlated by attaching strain gage nearby package corner. The preliminary result shows that the maximum stress and solder joint failure location are the consistent with experimental data. The influence on solder joint stress by different underfill material property, dispensing area and ball layout will be also considered into this study. Full array pattern of solder balls, high modulus underfill, and thinner package z-height can be beneficial in reducing solder joint stress.

articleTitle: Study on the Strain Sensor Using Bended Optical Fiber
abstract: We prototyped a sensor in which the fiber was repeatedly bent. The sensor model is analyzed using the finite element method to clarify the behavior of the optical fiber inside the sensor.

articleTitle: Temperature Distribution Measurement System for a Water-Cooled CPO Daughter Board
abstract: We build a thermal simulation model and a temperature distribution measurement system for a CPO daughter board which accommodates 32 ultra-compact optical transceivers. Our unique water-cooling system prevent providing the heat of switch ASIC to the optical transceivers. A targeted case temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{40}{{}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}}$</tex>, in order to keep a VCSEL temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq \mathbf{50}{{}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}}$</tex>, can be obtained even a 1.6-Tb/s optical transceiver consumes 6.4 W by adopting the water-cooled system operated with a water temperature of 30 °C and a water flow rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq \mathbf{1}.\mathbf{5}$</tex> L/min.

articleTitle: A Review of the Packaging Scheme of a Traction Inverter: Layout, Capacitor, Current Sensing and Power Module
abstract: A traction inverter is required to drive the AC motors found in electric vehicles, by means of DC/AC conversion. To achieve high power density and reliability, advancements in power electronics for inverters are highly required in the automotive market. Advances in power electronics and packaging have enabled these inverters to be highly reliable, cost efficient, have a higher power density and be more suited to the mass market. This paper presents an independent review of the BMW iX3 inverter. It will first focus on the overall configuration and layout of components inside the inverter. Then, the focus will be shifted to individual components such as the DC capacitors, current sensors, and power module. The aim of this paper is to provide an in-depth review of the inverter, which would prove a useful resource for an engineer designing an inverter or related components.

articleTitle: A D-Band Waveguide-Feed Patch Array on GaAs IPD Process
abstract: A D-band WR-6 waveguide-feed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 4$</tex> series type patch array using GaAs substrate integrated passive device (IPD) process is realized in this paper. The array comprised by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 4$</tex> series type patch, a transition of microstrip-to-substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW), and a right angle transition of SIW-to-WR-6 waveguide. A dielectric resonator (DR) is used for improve the bandwidth and reduce the loss of the transition of SIW-to-WR-6 waveguide. The proposed waveguide-feed patch array sis well suited for Sub-THz integrated system modules.

articleTitle: Study on Power Transmission System for a Dynamic Charging System Shared Between Light-Duty and Heavy-Duty Vehicles
abstract: In this paper, a method to stimulate a coil array-type dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) system, in which each coil is equipped with an independent inverter and the current amplitude is adjusted according to the coupling coefficient, has been proposed.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Power Module Structure (Cupper Clip Thickness) on Reliability Under Power Cycling Test
abstract: Power module is required to be high power density, high current, high reliability and low loss. Especially for xEV fields, high power density and high current are important. Therefore this paper presents the packaging technologies of enhanced reliability for high power density and high current module.
